title: March 2026 Governor & Lieutenant Governor Reshuffle
shortDescription: President Droupadi Murmu approved a reshuffle of Governors and Lieutenant Governors across nine states/UTs in early March 2026, ahead of that year's state assembly elections.
genZNote: Nine states, one reshuffle — you don't need every name, just the shape: who moved where, and that it's the President who signs off (Articles 153-162).

sections.heading: What Happened
sections.body: In early March 2026, President Droupadi Murmu approved a significant reshuffle of Governors and Lieutenant Governors across nine states and Union Territories, widely reported as timed ahead of that year's state assembly elections.

sections.heading: Key Facts
bullets: R. N. Ravi, then Governor of Tamil Nadu, was appointed Governor of West Bengal (effective 12 March 2026), succeeding C. V. Ananda Bose.
Kavinder Gupta, then Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, was sworn in as Governor of Himachal Pradesh (10 March 2026).
Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, Governor of Kerala, was given additional charge of Tamil Nadu.
Vinai Kumar Saxena, Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, was appointed Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh (succeeding Kavinder Gupta).
Former diplomat Taranjit Singh Sandhu was appointed Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.
Nand Kishore Yadav (former Bihar Assembly Speaker) was appointed Governor of Nagaland; Lt Gen (Retd) Syed Ata Hasnain was appointed Governor of Bihar.
The Governor's office is defined under Articles 153-162 of the Constitution — a direct link to the Constitution's chapter on state executives.

sections.heading: Why It Matters
sections.body: Governor and Lt. Governor appointments are a recurring 'Important Appointments' category, and this reshuffle is a useful case study connecting current affairs to the Constitution of India's Article 153-162 provisions on the office of Governor.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: President Murmu approved a reshuffle of Governors/Lt. Governors across nine states and UTs in early March 2026, ahead of assembly elections in several states.
keyFacts: R. N. Ravi: Tamil Nadu → West Bengal Governor (12 March 2026).
Kavinder Gupta: Ladakh LG → Himachal Pradesh Governor.
Vinai Kumar Saxena: Delhi LG → Ladakh LG; Taranjit Singh Sandhu → Delhi LG.
commonConfusion: A 'Governor' (states) and a 'Lieutenant Governor' (certain Union Territories) are different constitutional offices — this reshuffle moved people between both types.

highYieldFacts: The Governor's office is governed by Articles 153-162 of the Constitution — link this reshuffle directly to that chapter.
commonTraps: Mixing up which individual moved to which specific state in a nine-state reshuffle — focus on the two or three most-cited moves (R. N. Ravi to West Bengal is the highest-profile one) rather than memorising all nine.
mustRemember: R. N. Ravi became Governor of West Bengal in March 2026, succeeding C. V. Ananda Bose.
